mechanisms.title: Uncovered annulus diameters below 21 mm and above 27 mm (annulus-coverage)
mechanisms.explanation: All 93 no-fit hearts fail the annulus-coverage rule because the design only covers annulus diameters from 21 mm to 27 mm (sizes 23, 25, and 27). Grouping by annulusMm band shows that 6 no-fit hearts are in the 18-20 mm band and 20 no-fit hearts are in the 20-22 mm band (below the 21 mm minimum limit, e.g., heart-013 with annulusMm 20.3602109283815 against limit 21, margin -0.639789071618548), while 30 no-fit hearts are in the 26-28 mm band, 31 are in the 28-30 mm band, and 6 are in the 30-32 mm band (above the 27 mm maximum limit, e.g., heart-019 with annulusMm 27.3588421207855 against limit 27, margin -0.358842120785503). Profiling all 93 no-fit hearts shows higher group means in lvotMm (26.2397743438473 vs 23.5893006765396, effectSize 0.78842208254492) and annulusMm (26.1196504829399 vs 24.1814269470922, effectSize 0.783682598813269) because the majority of uncovered hearts lie above the 27 mm upper bound.

52 hearts are placed at risk by the stj-excess rule across all three valve sizes (23, 25, and 27 mm). Profiling this group shows a markedly smaller sinotubularJunctionMm than the rest of the cohort (groupMean 26.5045097370466 vs restMean 30.0246399161251, difference -3.52013017907853, effectSize -1.2156114728117), along with a smaller sinusMm (groupMean 30.5892482692222 vs restMean 33.1623513220977, effectSize -0.772725978362664) and higher lvotOverAnnulusAreaRatio (groupMean 1.02645440665182 vs restMean 0.953344983673109, effectSize 0.682085964814614). Individual heart inspections show that the stj-excess rule requires sinotubularJunctionMm to be at least 25 mm for size 23 (e.g., heart-018 has sinotubularJunctionMm 23.9075688982299 vs limit 25), 27 mm for size 25 (e.g., heart-025 has sinotubularJunctionMm 26.1350493604731 vs limit 27), and 29 mm for size 27 (e.g., heart-014 has sinotubularJunctionMm 26.8311463740637 and heart-001 has 28.5705544474013 vs limit 29). When a heart with a narrow sinotubular junction is assigned a larger nominal valve size based on its annulusMm, its STJ fails to meet the size-dependent threshold.
mechanisms.title: Narrow sinotubular junction relative to assigned valve size (stj-excess)

mechanisms.explanation: 38 hearts are placed at risk by the sinus-clearance rule across all three valve sizes (23, 25, and 27 mm). Profiling this group reveals significantly smaller sinusMm than the rest of the cohort (groupMean 29.0481355368023 vs restMean 33.2246133140638, difference -4.17647777726146, effectSize -1.25423382205296), smaller sinotubularJunctionMm (groupMean 26.7830986506325 vs restMean 29.8592581447899, effectSize -1.06229445590425), shorter sinusHeightMm (groupMean 22.0921052631579 vs restMean 25.4958563535912, effectSize -1.02110774508236), and higher lvotOverAnnulusAreaRatio (groupMean 1.02620177062988 vs restMean 0.956198939724312, effectSize 0.653102521023595). Individual heart inspections show that sinus-clearance requires sinusMm to be at least 28 mm for size 23 (e.g., heart-032 has sinusMm 27.1853980884363 and heart-018 has 26.3006749541182 vs limit 28), 30 mm for size 25 (e.g., heart-098 has sinusMm 29.566551695112 vs limit 30), and 32 mm for size 27 (e.g., heart-014 has sinusMm 30.7778575461286 vs limit 32). Hearts with narrow sinuses relative to their annulus-assigned nominal valve size fail to meet the required sinus clearance limit.
